summary: The season read's EXPLAIN test does not EXPLAIN the season read (duplicated SQL)
description:
**The season read's `EXPLAIN` test does not EXPLAIN the season read.**

Found by the Codex adversarial review of PR #44 (TKT-64) and verified against HEAD. Incidental to a
docs-only ticket, so filed rather than fixed there.

`TestGetPublishedSeasonIsIndexScoped` (`services/catalog/internal/store/season_smoke_test.go`) is
TKT-60's evidence that a season read is scoped by *physical scan cost* rather than merely returning
the right rows. It EXPLAINs a **hand-copied, reduced** query:

```sql
SELECT p.id FROM performances p
JOIN events e ON e.id = p.event_id
WHERE p.status = 'published' AND ($1::uuid[] IS NULL OR e.id = ANY($1))
```

The production read (`publicPerformances`, `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go`) joins four
more tables (`venues`, `ticket_types`, `series_performances`, `series`), projects ~24 columns, and
sorts by a `COALESCE` expression. **The two SQL texts are duplicated, not shared.**

**Why it matters.** The test proves the *predicate is index-compatible* — that
`performances_by_event` can serve `status` + `event_id = ANY(…)` under seeded statistics. It does
not prove the shipped query's plan uses that index. `publicPerformances` can drift to a
catalog-wide scan — the exact TKT-60 defect regressing — while this test stays green, because it
is not testing that query. The joins and the sort are precisely the kind of thing that flips a
planner.

**This is the failure mode the test was written to prevent, one level up.** TKT-53's test asserted
the output and would have passed against unfixed code; this test asserts a plan, but not *the*
plan. ADR-019 rule 2 (TKT-64) now documents the gap explicitly rather than claiming coverage the
test doesn't provide.

**COS:** the plan assertion binds to the SQL the season read actually executes — the query text is
shared between `publicPerformances` and the test (extracted to a constant/builder, or exposed via a
test seam) rather than retyped, so editing the production query is what the `EXPLAIN` test reads.
Sabotage-verify it: change the production query's scoping predicate (or drop
`performances_by_event`) and confirm the test goes red — the old duplicated-SQL version stays green
through the same sabotage, which is the point. `TestGetPublishedSeasonDoesNotScanForeignEvents`
stays green and unchanged. Then narrow or remove ADR-019's "rule currently outruns its enforcement"
consequence to match what the test then proves. `make check` green.

**Note:** the fix is a real judgement call, not mechanical — sharing a 14-line query string between
production and a smoke test can couple the test to formatting noise. `EXPLAIN`ing the exact
production text is the goal; how the text gets shared is open. Worth a plan gate.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=blocker -->
**TKT-63 (PR #46) has almost certainly done this ticket's job. Read before picking it up — do not
start work here without re-scoping it first.** Posted by the TKT-63 run, 2026-07-15.

**What happened.** TKT-63's `ai-review` (gpt-5.6-sol) independently rediscovered this exact gap and
filed it as blocking TKT-63 — on the grounds that TKT-63's own COS ("the scoped read keeps index
scans under `force_generic_plan`") could not be discharged by EXPLAINing a surrogate. It was right,
so it was fixed in PR #46 rather than deferred to here.

**This ticket's premise is void.** The filing says:

> the fix is a real judgement call, not mechanical — sharing a 14-line query string between
> production and a smoke test can couple the test to formatting noise. **Worth a plan gate.**

That was true of the *old* code, where the query was a literal built inside `publicPerformances`.
TKT-63 split it into composed consts, so the test now passes `scopedPublicPerformancesQuery` — the
exact statement the season read executes — straight to `explainGenericPlan`. **Nothing is retyped,
so there is no formatting coupling to judge.** The judgement call this ticket was gated on does not
exist any more. This is the sequencing bet from the TKT-63 claim comment paying off, and then some:
the enabler turned out to *be* the fix.

**COS-by-COS against what PR #46 shipped:**

| TKT-65 COS | status in PR #46 |
|---|---|
| plan assertion binds to the SQL the season read actually executes | ✅ EXPLAINs `scopedPublicPerformancesQuery` itself |
| query text shared, not retyped (const/builder/test seam) | ✅ composed consts; the test references the const |
| sabotage-verify: regress the production query → test goes red | ✅ two sabotages, both red — the nullable `OR`, **and** re-assembling the scoped query around the *unscoped* predicate (a construction-level regression the old surrogate stayed green through) |
| `TestGetPublishedSeasonDoesNotScanForeignEvents` stays green and unchanged | ✅ untouched |
| narrow/remove ADR-019's "rule currently outruns its enforcement" consequence | ✅ replaced — rule 2 is now a **gate** for the season read, explicitly **not** generalised (see below) |
| `make check` green | ✅ |

**What is genuinely left — and it is not what this ticket says.** One real remainder, deliberately
*not* folded into TKT-63 because it is a different read with a different index and its own evidence:

- **`GetPublishedFestival` (TKT-53) still has only a result-scope test.** No `EXPLAIN` assertion at
  all. ADR-019 rule 2 therefore remains an undischarged standard *there* — the festival read could
  drift to a catalog scan and nothing would redden. PR #46's ADR edit says exactly this rather than
  claiming the gap is closed everywhere.

**Recommendation for the human:** once PR #46 merges, either **close this ticket** as delivered by
TKT-63, or **re-scope it** to "give `GetPublishedFestival` the plan assertion rule 2 owes it"
(`performances_capacity_group_idx`, 0006) — which is a genuinely different ticket wearing this
ticket's number. Re-scoping is the better option: the festival gap is real and currently untracked
by anything else. Either way this ticket must not be worked as written.

**Note:** this comment records a scope change, not a transition. TKT-65 stays in `Backlog` and stays
the human's to prioritise; PR #46 is still at Gate 3 and could yet change.
